title: Positive feedback, quenching, and sequential super star cluster (SSC) formation in NGC 4945
question: How do the formation and early evolution of Super Star Clusters (SSCs) in NGC 4945 proceed, and to what extent does positive feedback from the molecular outflow trigger sequential SSC formation versus quenching?

what.value: Catalog of 27 SSC regions, gas mass estimates, stellar mass / L_ZAMS from 90 GHz radio continuum emission

evidence.quote: This tool uses the molecular spectroscopy in the publicly available molecular catalogues CDMS ((cite: Muller01)) and JPL ((cite: Pickett98)).

recipe.goal: Select sample of 14 Super Star Clusters (SSCs) across evolutionary stages
recipe.method: Select 14 SSCs out of 27 in Emig et al. (2020) by peak emission of vibrationally excited HC3N,v71 or HCN*, and by dust continuum peak at ~350 GHz with only CS and ground-state HC3N emissions and high stellar mass (10^5.1 - 10^5.7 M_sun)
key_parameters: Stellar mass range 10^5.1 - 10^5.7 M_sun; gas mass threshold 10^5.0 M_sun

recipe.goal: Identify molecular lines and fit LTE line profiles to derive rotational and vibrational temperatures (T_rot and T_vib)
recipe.method: Simulate line profiles under LTE conditions including opacity effects for a given source size using MADCUBA SLIM; derive T_vib from transitions with the same J across different vibrational states, and T_rot from rotational transitions within the same vibrational state (or from CS and HC3N,v0)
assumptions: Local Thermodynamic Equilibrium (LTE); T_vib ~ T_dust because HC3N* is mid-IR pumped and mid-IR dust emission is optically thick

recipe.goal: Estimate lower and upper limits to the proto-SSC sizes
recipe.method: Estimate lower limit to proto-HC3N size from line intensities of v71 rotational transitions assuming optically thick emission; for non-detections of HC3N*, derive upper limit to size from HC3N,v0 line intensity assuming the T_vib upper limit
assumptions: Optically thick emission for v71 transitions; D ~ 3.8 Mpc

recipe.goal: Derive apparent and greenhouse-corrected protostellar luminosities (L_p*), protostellar masses (M_p*), and SSC evolutionary ages (t_age)
recipe.method: Compute apparent luminosity via Stefan-Boltzmann law L_app = 4 * pi * r^2 * sigma * T_vib^4; apply greenhouse correction factor 4/psi ~ 1/10 to get L_p* = (4/psi) * L_app; estimate ages from L_p*/L_ZAMS using t_age = 10^5 / (1 + L_p*/L_ZAMS) yr
key_parameters: Greenhouse correction factor 4/psi ~ 1/10; HII region timescale ~ 10^5 yr
assumptions: N(H2) of a few 10^24 cm^-2; SHC density profile power-law index between 1 and 2; light-to-mass ratio of 10^3 L_sun M_sun^-1

recipe.goal: Analyze spatial distribution of SSCs relative to the molecular outflow and correlate T_rot with SSC evolutionary age
recipe.method: Correlate T_rot(v0) with t_age and compare deprojected galactocentric distances of SSCs with the CO molecular outflow lobes from Bolatto et al. (2021)
assumptions: Inner disk inclination of ~62 deg from Chou et al. (2007)
